brique._comment: Engine-native Reflexive family capacity. kind/wrapper/rel_ctx/lang do not apply here.

objective.name: read.structure
objective.description: Read the deterministic context structure tree from the local filesystem view.

#root.role: Traverse the local context tree from disk, normalize scope and traversal limits, and return the resulting structure tree.

scope._comment: Optional child context name relative to the addressed context. When provided, traversal starts from that child.

depth._comment: Optional traversal depth. 0 (default) returns only context nodes recursively without content. A positive value N includes context contents and descends at most N context levels.

max_per_path._comment: Optional maximum number of items returned per directory node. Defaults to an engine limit when absent.

root._comment: Root navigation node. Recursive structure: { name (string), kind (string), children (array of nodes) }. Possible kind values: 'context' (a context directory), 'context_file' (context.json itself), 'dir' (a Brique directory entry: capacity/, matter/, structure/, document/, schema/, code/, ui/), 'capacity' (an individual capacity file inside capacity/), 'matter_item' (an individual matter inside matter/), 'structure_item' (an individual structure inside structure/), 'document' (an individual document inside document/), 'schema' (an individual schema inside schema/), 'file' (a raw file inside code/ or ui/). Note: directory container nodes (capacity/, matter/, etc.) always have kind='dir'; their children have the specific kind (capacity, matter_item, etc.).

params._comment: Effective traversal parameters applied: { scope (string), depth (integer), max_per_path (integer) }.

effects.context_tree: The local context filesystem is scanned as the authoritative source of structural information.

transformation_contract.morphing: A structure query over the local context tree becomes a deterministic structural snapshot with explicit effective traversal parameters.
invariants: The current context filesystem is the authoritative source for traversal results.
depth is normalized to a non-negative value and max_per_path is clamped to a positive limit before traversal.
depth zero returns only context nodes and recursively traverses the complete descendant context hierarchy.
depth greater than zero includes context contents and bounds descendant context traversal to the requested depth.
When scope is provided, it must resolve to a local child context under the current context root.

Directory container nodes (capacity/, matter/, structure/, document/, schema/, code/, ui/) always have kind='dir'. Their children have specific kinds (capacity, matter_item, structure_item, document, schema, file).
matter and structure directory nodes are only included when their directory physically exists on disk.
code/ and ui/ directories are scanned recursively; files within them use kind: 'file'.
build/, tmp/, trace/ and other non-Brique directories are excluded from traversal.
success: On success, read.structure returns a root navigation node plus the effective normalized query parameters.
With depth zero, every returned node has kind context and no context content nodes are returned.
Successful traversal returns deterministic sibling ordering and per-path truncation metadata when child lists exceed max_per_path.
failure: The capacity fails when scope is invalid, missing on disk, or does not designate a context child.
The capacity fails when local descriptor or filesystem access needed for traversal cannot be completed.
notes: The payload is a structural navigation snapshot, not a runtime state snapshot.
Matter and structure listings are derived from local disk layout rather than from remote or projected state.

A bounded depth (depth > 0, or scope narrowing traversal to a subtree) means a missing element in the result is not evidence the element doesn't exist — it may simply live deeper than the requested depth, or outside the requested scope. depth=0 traverses the complete descendant context hierarchy (see invariant above) and does not have this blind spot for contexts, but even then content nodes (capacity/matter/document/etc.) are never returned at depth=0, so an element's content-level absence there is equally inconclusive. When searching for a specific named element and the traversal depth needed to find it is unknown in advance, prefer meaning.query or the vocabulary capacities (name-based lookup, unbounded by tree position) over increasing depth speculatively.
